draft.title: Enlightenment ideas in America
card: The Enlightenment was a European movement of the 1600s and 1700s. It said that reason could be used to understand people and to improve government.
rights that people have by birth, not by gift of a ruler. John Locke named them as life, liberty and property.
government gets its authority from the agreement of the people it governs. If a government abuses their rights, Locke argued, the people may replace it.
Educated colonists read Locke and, from 1776, Thomas Paine's pamphlet Common Sense. They used these ideas to argue that British rule over them was unjust.
draft.remember: Natural rights and consent gave colonists a way to argue that British rule was unjust.

a.q: A colonist says: 'Government has no right to rule us without our agreement.' Which Enlightenment idea is this?
opts: Government by consent
Natural rights of birth
The divine right of kings
Trade regulation by Parliament
a.why: The idea that a government's authority comes from the agreement of the governed is government by consent. Natural rights are about what people hold from birth, such as life and liberty, not about where a government's authority comes from.
a.clue: Where does a government's authority come from?

b.q: In 1774, Hannah, a printer in Philadelphia, reads Locke and argues that Britain's actions break the rights colonists hold from birth. How does this reading shape her thinking?
opts: It gives her a principle to call British rule unjust
It proves that Parliament has no legal power at all
It forces her to join the colonial resistance
It shows her that Britain will soon grant independence
b.why: Locke's ideas gave colonists like Hannah a principle: rights come from birth, so a government that ignores them can be judged unjust. Ideas can shape a person's thinking, but the card does not say they forced anyone to act or proved a legal point.
b.clue: The ideas shaped how colonists argued, not what they had to do.

b.best: It gives her a principle to call British rule unjust
